## Data Cleaning

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# Script: Normalize SurveyMonkey Survey Responses
# Purpose: Consolidate multiple answer columns into single columns per question
# ============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(stringr)

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: Read the raw data
# ============================================================================

# Read without headers first
raw_data <- read_csv(
  "CSV/Customer Survey 2025 English Online.csv",
  col_names = FALSE,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

cat("Original dimensions:", nrow(raw_data), "rows x", ncol(raw_data), "columns\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: Extract questions and answer options
# ============================================================================

# Row 1: Questions (some columns are empty, meaning they belong to previous question)
questions <- raw_data[1, ] %>% unlist() %>% as.character()

# Row 2: Answer options for each column
answers <- raw_data[2, ] %>% unlist() %>% as.character()

# Row 3+: Actual response data
response_data <- raw_data[-c(1, 2), ]

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: Identify question groups
# ============================================================================

# Fill empty question cells with the previous non-empty question
# This groups columns that belong to the same question
current_question <- ""
question_groups <- character(length(questions))

for (i in seq_along(questions)) {
  if (!is.na(questions[i]) && questions[i] != "") {
    current_question <- questions[i]
  }
  question_groups[i] <- current_question
}

# Create a mapping dataframe
column_mapping <- tibble(
  col_index = 1:length(questions),
  question = question_groups,
  answer_option = answers
) %>%
  filter(question != "")  # Remove any columns with no question

cat("\nFound", length(unique(column_mapping$question)), "unique questions\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: Consolidate columns for each question
# ============================================================================

# Function to consolidate multiple columns into one
consolidate_columns <- function(data, indices, answer_labels) {
  # Get the columns for this question
  cols <- data[, indices, drop = FALSE]
  
  # FIX: Clean NA labels for detection logic
  answer_labels_clean <- replace_na(answer_labels, "") 
  
  # Check if this is an open-ended question
  is_open_ended <- any(str_detect(answer_labels_clean, "(?i)open.?ended|please specify|optional|self.?describe|self.?identify"))
  
  # For each row, find which column has a value and return that answer option
  result <- apply(cols, 1, function(row) {
    # Find non-empty values
    non_empty <- which(!is.na(row) & row != "")
    
    if (length(non_empty) == 0) {
      return(NA_character_)
    } else if (is_open_ended) {
      # For open-ended questions, return the actual text value(s)
      text_values <- row[non_empty]
      # Remove any that are just "X" or checkmarks
      text_values <- text_values[!text_values %in% c("X", "x", "✓", "✔")]
      if (length(text_values) == 0) {
        return(NA_character_)
      }
      return(paste(text_values, collapse = "; "))
    } else if (length(non_empty) == 1) {
      # Single answer - check if it's actual text or just a checkmark
      value <- row[non_empty]
      if (value %in% c("X", "x", "✓", "✔") || is.na(value)) {
        # It's a checkmark, return the answer option label
        return(answer_labels[non_empty])
      } else {
        # It's actual text, return it
        return(value)
      }
    } else {
      # Multiple answers (e.g., "select all that apply")
      selected_labels <- c()
      selected_text <- c()
      
      for (i in non_empty) {
        value <- row[i]
        if (value %in% c("X", "x", "✓", "✔")) {
          # It's a checkmark
          selected_labels <- c(selected_labels, answer_labels[i])
        } else {
          # It's text
          selected_text <- c(selected_text, value)
        }
      }
      
      # Combine both
      all_values <- c(selected_labels, selected_text)
      return(paste(all_values, collapse = "; "))
    }
  })
  
  return(result)
}

# Create normalized dataset
normalized_data <- tibble()
open_ended_count <- 0

# Process each unique question
unique_questions <- unique(column_mapping$question)

cat("\nProcessing questions...\n")

for (q in unique_questions) {
  # Get all columns for this question
  q_mapping <- column_mapping %>% filter(question == q)
  
  # Extract indices and answer labels
  indices <- q_mapping$col_index
  answer_labels <- q_mapping$answer_option
  
  # FIX: Clean NA labels for detection logic
  answer_labels_clean <- replace_na(answer_labels, "") 
  
  # Check if open-ended (THIS IS WHERE THE ORIGINAL ERROR OCCURRED)
  if (any(str_detect(answer_labels_clean, "(?i)open.?ended|please specify|optional|self.?describe|self.?identify"))) {
    open_ended_count <- open_ended_count + 1
  }
  
  # Consolidate into single column
  # Use the original answer_labels for selection logic, but the cleaned version for detection
  consolidated <- consolidate_columns(response_data, indices, answer_labels) 
  
  # Add to normalized dataset
  if (ncol(normalized_data) == 0) {
    normalized_data <- tibble(!!q := consolidated)
  } else {
    normalized_data[[q]] <- consolidated
  }
  
  if (match(q, unique_questions) %% 10 == 0) {
    cat("  Processed", match(q, unique_questions), "of", length(unique_questions), "questions\n")
  }
}

cat("\nFound", open_ended_count, "open-ended questions\n")
cat("Normalized dimensions:", nrow(normalized_data), "rows x", ncol(normalized_data), "columns\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: Clean up column names
# ============================================================================

# Shorten very long question names and make them valid R names
clean_colnames <- colnames(normalized_data) %>%
  str_trunc(100, ellipsis = "...") %>%  # Limit length
  make.names() %>%  # Make valid R names
  make.unique()  # Ensure uniqueness

colnames(normalized_data) <- clean_colnames

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: Save the normalized data
# ============================================================================

# Save as CSV
write_csv(
  normalized_data,
  "Output/normalized_survey_responses.csv"
)

cat("\nNormalized data saved to: normalized_survey_responses.csv\n")

# Save as RDS
saveRDS(
  normalized_data,
  "Output/normalized_survey_responses.rds"
)

cat("Also saved as RDS file: normalized_survey_responses.rds\n")

# Save the mapping for reference
write_csv(
  column_mapping,
  "Output/question_answer_mapping.csv"
)

cat("Question-answer mapping saved to: question_answer_mapping.csv\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 7: Summary and preview
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Total responses:", nrow(normalized_data), "\n")
cat("Total questions:", ncol(normalized_data), "\n")

cat("\n=== SAMPLE QUESTIONS ===\n")
sample_qs <- head(colnames(normalized_data), 10)
for (i in seq_along(sample_qs)) {
  cat(i, ":", sample_qs[i], "\n")
}

cat("\n=== DATA PREVIEW (First 5 rows, first 3 columns) ===\n")
print(normalized_data[1:5, 1:3])

# Count response rates
cat("\n=== RESPONSE RATES ===\n")
response_counts <- normalized_data %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(!is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Question", values_to = "Responses") %>%
  arrange(desc(Responses)) %>%
  head(10)

print(response_counts)

cat("\n✓ Script completed successfully!\n")
cat("✓ Each question is now in a single column\n")
cat("✓ Multiple selections are separated by semicolons (;)\n")
```



```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(scales)
library(gridExtra)
library(RColorBrewer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("Output/normalized_survey_responses.csv", 
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

columns_to_remove <- c("Respondent ID", "Respondent.ID", 
                       "Collector ID", "Collector.ID",
                       "Start Date", "Start.Date",
                       "End Date", "End.Date",
                       "IP Address", "IP.Address",
                       "Email Address", "Email.Address",
                       "First Name", "First.Name",
                       "Last Name", "Last.Name",
                       "Custom Data 1", "Custom.Data.1")

# Remove columns that match any of these names
data <- data %>%
  select(-any_of(columns_to_remove))

cat("After removing identifying columns:", ncol(data), "\n")
cat("Remaining columns:\n")
print(names(data))



# Create a more complete list of clean names for 46 columns
clean_names <- c(
  "tax_method", "site_location", "overall_experience", "enough_info",
  "future_scheduling", "financial_coaching_discussed", "felt_respected",
  "felt_included", "appointment_comments", "appointment_experience",
  "website_experience", "service_delivery_preference", "tax_info_source",
  "race_ethnicity", "gender", "sexual_identity", "age",
  "employment_status", "annual_income", "household_size", "children_under_18",
  "language_comfortable", "future_language_services", "disability_questions",
  "financial_challenges", "financial_goals", "advance_ctc_enrolled",
  "ctc_lump_sum", "advance_ctc_public_benefits", "future_ctc_likelihood",
  "ctc_info_needed", "no_enroll_reason", "ctc_use", "involvement_interest",
  "volunteer_barriers"
)

# Pad with generic names for any extra columns
if(ncol(data) > length(clean_names)) {
  extra_names <- paste0("extra_col_", 1:(ncol(data) - length(clean_names)))
  clean_names <- c(clean_names, extra_names)
}

# Assign column names
colnames(data) <- clean_names[1:ncol(data)]

cat("\nNew column names assigned:\n")
print(names(data))

#############################################
# DATA PREPROCESSING
#############################################

# Helper functions
satisfaction_map <- function(x) {
  if(is.na(x) || x == "") return(NA)
  if(grepl("Very positive", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(5)
  else if(grepl("Somewhat positive", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(4)
  else if(grepl("Neutral", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(3)
  else if(grepl("Somewhat negative", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(2)
  else if(grepl("Very negative", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(1)
  else return(NA)
}

income_to_numeric <- function(x) {
  if(is.na(x) || x == "" || x == "I prefer not to answer") return(NA)
  else if(x == "$0") return(0)
  else if(x == "$1-$4,999") return(2500)
  else if(x == "$5,000-$9,999") return(7500)
  else if(x == "$10,000-$19,999") return(15000)
  else if(x == "$20,000-$29,999") return(25000)
  else if(x == "$30,000-$39,999") return(35000)
  else if(x == "$40,000-$59,999") return(50000)
  else if(x == "$60,000+") return(70000)
  else return(NA)
}

simplify_race <- function(x) {
  if(is.na(x) || x == "") return(NA)
  else if(grepl("White or European Descent", x) & !grepl(";", x)) return("White")
  else if(grepl("Black or African American", x) & !grepl(";", x)) return("Black")
  else if(grepl("Asian or Asian American", x) & !grepl(";", x)) return("Asian")
  else if(grepl("Hispanic or Latino", x) & !grepl(";", x)) return("Hispanic/Latino")
  else if(grepl("American Indian or Alaska Native", x) & !grepl(";", x)) return("Native American")
  else if(grepl(";", x)) return("Multiracial")
  else return("Other")
}

respect_map <- function(x) {
  if(is.na(x) || x == "") return(NA)
  if(grepl("Very respected", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(5)
  else if(grepl("Somewhat respected", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(4)
  else if(grepl("Neutral", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(3)
  else if(grepl("Somewhat disrespected", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(2)
  else if(grepl("Very disrespected", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(1)
  else return(NA)
}

inclusion_map <- function(x) {
  if(is.na(x) || x == "") return(NA)
  if(grepl("Very included", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(5)
  else if(grepl("Somewhat included", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(4)
  else if(grepl("Neutral", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(3)
  else if(grepl("Somewhat excluded", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(2)
  else if(grepl("Very excluded", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) return(1)
  else return(NA)
}

# Check if required columns exist before processing
required_cols <- c("overall_experience", "felt_respected", "felt_included", 
                   "annual_income", "race_ethnicity", "age", "household_size", 
                   "children_under_18")

missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(data))
if(length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  cat("\nWarning: Missing columns:", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("Available columns:", paste(names(data), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  stop("Please verify column names match the data structure.")
}

# Apply transformations with better error handling
data_processed <- data %>%
  mutate(
    satisfaction_score = sapply(overall_experience, satisfaction_map),
    respect_score = sapply(felt_respected, respect_map),
    inclusion_score = sapply(felt_included, inclusion_map),
    income_numeric = sapply(annual_income, income_to_numeric),
    race_simple = sapply(race_ethnicity, simplify_race),
    age_numeric = as.numeric(as.character(age)),
    household_numeric = as.numeric(as.character(household_size)),
    children_numeric = as.numeric(as.character(children_under_18))
  )

# Create categorical variables separately
data_processed <- data_processed %>%
  mutate(
    age_group = cut(age_numeric, 
                    breaks = c(0, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 100),
                    labels = c("18-30", "31-40", "41-50", "51-60", "61-70", "70+")),
    
    income_bracket = case_when(
      income_numeric < 10000 ~ "Low (<$10k)",
      income_numeric >= 10000 & income_numeric < 20000 ~ "Low-Mid ($10-20k)",
      income_numeric >= 20000 & income_numeric < 30000 ~ "Middle ($20-30k)",
      income_numeric >= 30000 & income_numeric < 40000 ~ "Mid-High ($30-40k)",
      income_numeric >= 40000 ~ "High ($40k+)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    income_binary = ifelse(!is.na(income_numeric) & income_numeric < 20000, 
                          "Low Income (<$20k)", 
                          ifelse(!is.na(income_numeric), "Higher Income ($20k+)", NA_character_)),
    
    gender_clean = case_when(
      gender == "Female" ~ "Female",
      gender == "Male" ~ "Male",
      gender == "Non-binary" ~ "Non-binary",
      TRUE ~ "Other/NA"
    ),
    
    has_children = ifelse(!is.na(children_numeric) & children_numeric > 0, 
                         "Has Children", 
                         ifelse(!is.na(children_numeric), "No Children", NA_character_)),
    
    employment_simple = case_when(
      grepl("full-time", employment_status, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Full-time",
      grepl("part-time", employment_status, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Part-time",
      grepl("self-employed", employment_status, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Self-employed",
      grepl("Unemployed, looking", employment_status) ~ "Unemployed (seeking)",
      grepl("Unemployed, not looking", employment_status) ~ "Unemployed (not seeking)",
      TRUE ~ "Other/NA"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(income_bracket = factor(income_bracket, 
                                 levels = c("Low (<$10k)", "Low-Mid ($10-20k)", 
                                           "Middle ($20-30k)", "Mid-High ($30-40k)", 
                                           "High ($40k+)")))

# Replace data with processed version
data <- data_processed

# Filter for main analyses
data_main <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(race_simple), 
         race_simple != "Other",
         gender_clean %in% c("Female", "Male"),
         !is.na(income_bracket))

cat("\nData preprocessing complete!\n")
cat("Total rows:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Rows for main analysis:", nrow(data_main), "\n")
#############################################
# CREATE COMPREHENSIVE VISUALIZATIONS
#############################################

# Set theme
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
          theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
                axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
                legend.position = "right",
                panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

# Color palettes
race_colors <- brewer.pal(8, "Set2")
gender_colors <- c("Female" = "#E91E63", "Male" = "#2196F3", "Non-binary" = "#9C27B0")
income_colors <- brewer.pal(5, "RdYlGn")[5:1]

pdf("comprehensive_granular_analysis.pdf", width = 16, height = 10)

#############################################
# 1. SATISFACTION BY GENDER, RACE, AND INCOME
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 1: Satisfaction by Demographics...\n")

p1 <- data_main %>%
  group_by(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_satisfaction = mean(satisfaction_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 5) %>%  # Only show groups with 5+ respondents
  ggplot(aes(x = race_simple, y = mean_satisfaction, fill = income_bracket)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~gender_clean, ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = income_colors) +
  labs(title = "Satisfaction Score by Race, Gender, and Income Level",
       subtitle = "Mean satisfaction scores (1-5 scale) - Groups with 5+ respondents",
       x = "Race/Ethnicity",
       y = "Mean Satisfaction Score",
       fill = "Income Bracket") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 4.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", alpha = 0.5) +
  ylim(0, 5)

print(p1)

#############################################
# 2. INCOME DISTRIBUTION BY RACE AND GENDER
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 2: Income Distribution...\n")

p2 <- data_main %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = race_simple, y = income_numeric, fill = gender_clean)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gender_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(title = "Income Distribution by Race and Gender",
       subtitle = "Box plots showing median, quartiles, and outliers",
       x = "Race/Ethnicity",
       y = "Annual Income",
       fill = "Gender") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  coord_flip()

print(p2)

#############################################
# 3. AGE DISTRIBUTION BY GENDER, RACE, AND INCOME
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 3: Age Distribution by Demographics...\n")

p3 <- data_main %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age_numeric, fill = income_bracket)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  facet_grid(gender_clean ~ race_simple) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = income_colors) +
  labs(title = "Age Distribution by Gender, Race, and Income",
       subtitle = "Histogram showing age patterns across demographic groups",
       x = "Age (years)",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Income Bracket") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 9))

print(p3)

#############################################
# 4. RESPECT AND INCLUSION BY DEMOGRAPHICS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 4: Respect and Inclusion Scores...\n")

respect_inclusion_data <- data_main %>%
  group_by(race_simple, gender_clean, income_binary) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_respect = mean(respect_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_inclusion = mean(inclusion_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 5)

p4 <- respect_inclusion_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(mean_respect, mean_inclusion),
               names_to = "metric",
               values_to = "score") %>%
  mutate(metric = recode(metric, 
                        mean_respect = "Respect",
                        mean_inclusion = "Inclusion")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = race_simple, y = score, fill = metric)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  facet_grid(income_binary ~ gender_clean) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(title = "Respect and Inclusion Scores by Race, Gender, and Income",
       subtitle = "Mean scores (1-5 scale) for feeling respected and included",
       x = "Race/Ethnicity",
       y = "Mean Score",
       fill = "Metric") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8)) +
  ylim(0, 5)

print(p4)

#############################################
# 5. FINANCIAL CHALLENGES BY DEMOGRAPHICS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 5: Financial Challenges...\n")

# Parse financial challenges
challenges_parsed <- data_main %>%
  select(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket, financial_challenges) %>%
  filter(!is.na(financial_challenges), financial_challenges != "") %>%
  mutate(challenges_list = strsplit(as.character(financial_challenges), ";")) %>%
  unnest(challenges_list) %>%
  mutate(challenges_list = trimws(challenges_list)) %>%
  filter(challenges_list != "", 
         challenges_list != "NA",
         challenges_list != "None of the above",
         challenges_list != "Prefer not to answer")

# Get top 5 challenges
top_challenges <- challenges_parsed %>%
  count(challenges_list, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  pull(challenges_list)

p5 <- challenges_parsed %>%
  filter(challenges_list %in% top_challenges) %>%
  count(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket, challenges_list) %>%
  group_by(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = race_simple, y = pct, fill = challenges_list)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  facet_grid(income_bracket ~ gender_clean) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") +
  labs(title = "Top 5 Financial Challenges by Demographics",
       subtitle = "Percentage distribution within each demographic group",
       x = "Race/Ethnicity",
       y = "Percentage (%)",
       fill = "Challenge Type") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8))

print(p5)

#############################################
# 6. EMPLOYMENT STATUS BY DEMOGRAPHICS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 6: Employment Patterns...\n")

p6 <- data_main %>%
  filter(!is.na(employment_simple), employment_simple != "Other/NA") %>%
  count(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket, employment_simple) %>%
  group_by(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = income_bracket, y = pct, fill = employment_simple)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
  facet_grid(race_simple ~ gender_clean) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Employment Status by Race, Gender, and Income",
       subtitle = "Proportion of employment types within each group",
       x = "Income Bracket",
       y = "Proportion",
       fill = "Employment Status") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        strip.text.y = element_text(size = 8))

print(p6)

#############################################
# 7. HOUSEHOLD SIZE AND CHILDREN BY DEMOGRAPHICS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 7: Household Composition...\n")

p7 <- data_main %>%
  filter(!is.na(household_numeric), household_numeric <= 10) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = household_numeric, fill = has_children)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  facet_grid(income_binary ~ race_simple + gender_clean) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Has Children" = "#4CAF50", 
                               "No Children" = "#9E9E9E")) +
  labs(title = "Household Size Distribution by Demographics and Parental Status",
       subtitle = "Number of people in household across demographic groups",
       x = "Household Size",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Parental Status") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7))

print(p7)

#############################################
# 8. AGE VS INCOME BY RACE AND GENDER
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 8: Age-Income Relationship...\n")

p8 <- data_main %>%
  filter(!is.na(age_numeric), !is.na(income_numeric)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age_numeric, y = income_numeric, color = gender_clean)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, linewidth = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~race_simple, ncol = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = gender_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(title = "Age vs Income Relationship by Race and Gender",
       subtitle = "Scatter plot with LOESS smoothing curves",
       x = "Age (years)",
       y = "Annual Income",
       color = "Gender") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10))

print(p8)

#############################################
# 9. SATISFACTION TRENDS ACROSS AGE GROUPS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 9: Satisfaction by Age Groups...\n")

p9 <- data_main %>%
  filter(!is.na(age_group), !is.na(satisfaction_score)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age_group, y = satisfaction_score, fill = income_bracket)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(gender_clean ~ race_simple) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = income_colors) +
  labs(title = "Satisfaction Distribution Across Age Groups by Demographics",
       subtitle = "Box plots showing satisfaction variation by age, race, gender, and income",
       x = "Age Group",
       y = "Satisfaction Score",
       fill = "Income Bracket") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8))

print(p9)

#############################################
# 10. FINANCIAL GOALS BY DEMOGRAPHICS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 10: Financial Goals...\n")

goals_parsed <- data_main %>%
  select(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket, financial_goals) %>%
  filter(!is.na(financial_goals), financial_goals != "") %>%
  mutate(goals_list = strsplit(as.character(financial_goals), ";")) %>%
  unnest(goals_list) %>%
  mutate(goals_list = trimws(goals_list)) %>%
  filter(goals_list != "", 
         goals_list != "NA",
         goals_list != "Prefer not to answer")

# Get top 5 goals
top_goals <- goals_parsed %>%
  count(goals_list, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  pull(goals_list)

p10 <- goals_parsed %>%
  filter(goals_list %in% top_goals) %>%
  count(race_simple, income_bracket, goals_list) %>%
  group_by(race_simple, income_bracket) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = income_bracket, y = pct, fill = goals_list)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~race_simple, ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(title = "Top 5 Financial Goals by Race and Income Level",
       subtitle = "Percentage of respondents with each goal",
       x = "Income Bracket",
       y = "Percentage (%)",
       fill = "Financial Goal") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

print(p10)

#############################################
# 11. HEATMAP: SATISFACTION BY RACE AND INCOME
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 11: Satisfaction Heatmap...\n")

heatmap_data <- data_main %>%
  group_by(race_simple, income_bracket, gender_clean) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_satisfaction = mean(satisfaction_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 3)

p11 <- ggplot(heatmap_data, 
              aes(x = income_bracket, y = race_simple, fill = mean_satisfaction)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_satisfaction, 2)), 
            color = "black", size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~gender_clean) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#E74C3C", mid = "#F39C12", high = "#2ECC71",
                      midpoint = 4.5, limits = c(4, 5)) +
  labs(title = "Satisfaction Score Heatmap by Race, Income, and Gender",
       subtitle = "Numbers show mean satisfaction score (1-5 scale)",
       x = "Income Bracket",
       y = "Race/Ethnicity",
       fill = "Mean\nSatisfaction") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(p11)

#############################################
# 12. COMPLEX INTERACTION: SATISFACTION BY MULTIPLE FACTORS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 12: Complex Satisfaction Analysis...\n")

p12 <- data_main %>%
  filter(!is.na(satisfaction_score), !is.na(has_children)) %>%
  group_by(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket, has_children) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_satisfaction = mean(satisfaction_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(satisfaction_score, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 5) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = income_bracket, y = mean_satisfaction, 
             color = has_children, group = has_children)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_satisfaction - se, 
                    ymax = mean_satisfaction + se),
                width = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(gender_clean ~ race_simple) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Has Children" = "#E91E63", 
                               "No Children" = "#2196F3")) +
  labs(title = "Satisfaction by Income, Race, Gender, and Parental Status",
       subtitle = "Mean satisfaction with standard error bars (groups with 5+ respondents)",
       x = "Income Bracket",
       y = "Mean Satisfaction Score",
       color = "Parental Status") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8)) +
  ylim(4, 5)

print(p12)

#############################################
# 13. INCOME INEQUALITY VISUALIZATION
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 13: Income Inequality Analysis...\n")

income_stats <- data_main %>%
  group_by(race_simple, gender_clean) %>%
  summarise(
    median_income = median(income_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = quantile(income_numeric, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(income_numeric, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p13 <- ggplot(income_stats, 
              aes(x = race_simple, y = median_income, fill = gender_clean)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
                position = position_dodge(0.9), width = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gender_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(title = "Median Income by Race and Gender with Interquartile Range",
       subtitle = "Error bars show 25th to 75th percentile range",
       x = "Race/Ethnicity",
       y = "Median Annual Income",
       fill = "Gender") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  coord_flip()

print(p13)

#############################################
# 14. RESPECT-INCLUSION CORRELATION BY DEMOGRAPHICS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 14: Respect-Inclusion Correlation...\n")

p14 <- data_main %>%
  filter(!is.na(respect_score), !is.na(inclusion_score)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = respect_score, y = inclusion_score, color = income_bracket)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 1) +
  facet_grid(gender_clean ~ race_simple) +
  scale_color_manual(values = income_colors) +
  labs(title = "Respect vs Inclusion Scores by Race, Gender, and Income",
       subtitle = "Scatter plot with linear regression lines",
       x = "Respect Score",
       y = "Inclusion Score",
       color = "Income Bracket") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 9))

print(p14)

#############################################
# 15. SERVICE USAGE PATTERNS BY DEMOGRAPHICS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 15: Service Site Usage...\n")

site_data <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(site_location), site_location != "",
         !is.na(race_simple), race_simple != "Other",
         gender_clean %in% c("Female", "Male"),
         !is.na(income_binary)) %>%
  mutate(site_simple = case_when(
    grepl("Main Office, St. Paul", site_location) ~ "Main Office",
    grepl("VEAP, Bloomington", site_location) ~ "VEAP",
    grepl("CAPI, Brooklyn", site_location) ~ "CAPI",
    grepl("Merrick", site_location) ~ "Merrick",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  ))

p15 <- site_data %>%
  count(race_simple, gender_clean, income_binary, site_simple) %>%
  group_by(race_simple, gender_clean, income_binary) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = site_simple, y = pct, fill = income_binary)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  facet_grid(gender_clean ~ race_simple) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Low Income (<$20k)" = "#E74C3C",
                               "Higher Income ($20k+)" = "#2ECC71")) +
  labs(title = "Service Site Usage by Race, Gender, and Income",
       subtitle = "Percentage using each site within demographic groups",
       x = "Service Site",
       y = "Percentage (%)",
       fill = "Income Level") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8))

print(p15)

#############################################
# 16. AGE GROUP DISTRIBUTION BY ALL DEMOGRAPHICS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 16: Age Group Proportions...\n")

p16 <- data_main %>%
  filter(!is.na(age_group)) %>%
  count(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket, age_group) %>%
  group_by(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age_group, y = pct, fill = age_group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_grid(income_bracket ~ race_simple + gender_clean) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "YlOrRd") +
  labs(title = "Age Group Distribution by Race, Gender, and Income",
       subtitle = "Percentage distribution within each demographic combination",
       x = "Age Group",
       y = "Percentage (%)",
       fill = "Age Group") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 6),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 6),
        legend.position = "bottom")

print(p16)

#############################################
# 17. MULTIDIMENSIONAL SATISFACTION ANALYSIS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 17: Multidimensional Satisfaction...\n")

multi_satisfaction <- data_main %>%
  filter(!is.na(satisfaction_score), !is.na(age_group)) %>%
  group_by(race_simple, gender_clean, income_bracket, age_group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_satisfaction = mean(satisfaction_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 3)

p17 <- ggplot(multi_satisfaction, 
              aes(x = age_group, y = mean_satisfaction, 
                  color = income_bracket, group = income_bracket)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_grid(gender_clean ~ race_simple) +
  scale_color_manual(values = income_colors) +
  labs(title = "Satisfaction Trends Across Age by Race, Gender, and Income",
       subtitle = "Mean satisfaction scores showing age patterns (groups with 3+ respondents)",
       x = "Age Group",
       y = "Mean Satisfaction Score",
       color = "Income Bracket") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8)) +
  ylim(4, 5)

print(p17)

#############################################
# 18. INCOME DISPARITY ANALYSIS
#############################################
cat("Creating Plot 18: Income Disparity Visualization...\n")

p18 <- data_main %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = race_simple, y = income_numeric, fill = gender_clean)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.6, scale = "width") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.9), 
               outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8) +

  labs(title = "Income Distribution Patterns by Race and Gender",
       subtitle = "Violin plots show distribution density; box plots show quartiles",
       x = "Race/Ethnicity",
       y = "Annual Income",
       fill = "Gender") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  coord_flip()

print(p18)
```
